DecentraWorld was founded in 2021 by a group of whitehat developers who believe in financial privacy, and freedom.

Today, DecentraWorld decided that it would only has its way and rugged its project taking away over $1M. The deployer accumulated tax and transaction fees in the form of DecentraWorld tokens from DEWO’s token transfers, and sold 31,825,441 of those tokens.

The bulk of the funds still remains at 0x3b9DcFe447f9102EE358daad0EE4d1EcF7039991. The project was KYC'ed and its smart contract was audited by SolidProof with 'flying color!'

Some smaller amounts ~ 279k was sent to FixedFLow Exchange and Pancakeswap into BUSD. This is a slow rug because the deployer last created the contract 29 days ago.

reports.category: Report Miscellaneous Crypto Scams with Chainabuse
reports.description: On May 4 2022, Mad Meerkat Finance (MMF), a DEX on Cronos, suffered a Domain Name Service (DNS) Hi-jacking. Approximately $2 million USD of blockchain assets were stolen [1]. The suspect used wallet (0xb3...9A6b) then bridge the funds from Cronos to Ethereum using the Multichain Bridge [2], and subsequently laundered the funds using Tornado Cash [3]. Analytics using blockchain data revealed 828 ETH withdrawn out of Tornado Cash to 4 suspected withdrawal addresses [4]. The funds were then transferred to 16 addresses associated with FixedFloat Exchange and 1 address to the Binance CEX [5]. Substantial progress has since been made on this case, but due to jurisdictional and legal constraints the case is unable to move forward without a victim based in the United States coming forward. Thus, the potential recovery in approximately ~$2 million worth of digital assets depends on at least one US based victim willing to report the crime.

reports.category: Phishing Scams: Stay Protected on Chainabuse
reports.description:
Twitter user @ysiu reported on January 25th that his son had fallen for a Discord phishing scam and lost three valuable NFTs. The scammers, who used the Discord ID Callum#3640, apparently used a URL designed to impersonate Sudoswap to phish the victim. 

A review of the scammer's address indicates many more victims lost assets. Total swapped value of the stolen NFTs is approximately 36.75 ETH/$92,000 at the time of the thefts.

A further review of the scammer's address indicates most of the stolen ETH were subsequently forwarded to 0xb2a8b37b1fc3fc0c41ec7d72adcfd47bf85f34c0 before being deposited to Tornado Cash. That address has processed 694 ETH during its active trading life (from October 2021 to April 2022).
